phases.name: Local capture + drawing engine, no cloud

tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-08-16 (82/82). Built ahead of 1.3's device verification on explicit owner instruction ("start what you can now, easiest to hardest") — this task doesn't touch native code or WebGL, so it isn't at risk from a camera-plugin rethink the way 2.2+ would be. tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a document with a camera Cel and a drawn Cel on top is rendered THE SYSTEM SHALL show both composited correctly, with no color halos or orientation mismatch.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-07. Visual verification done headlessly (Playwright + SwiftShader, this environment has no physical device either) via a new RendererHarness component (window.__clumsyloop) and scripts/renderer-smoke.mjs, reading back with renderer.toImageData() rather than a canvas screenshot — same preserveDrawingBuffer:false trap Trace's CLAUDE.md documents. Checks a four-quadrant synthetic photo (catches an orientation flip a solid color couldn't) with a real StrokeBuilder-generated pencil stroke composited on top: all four quadrants keep their own color, the stroke reads clearly darker than the photo under it, and the area just beside the stroke matches the plain photo color with no dark fringe. A screenshot for human eyeballing confirms the same by eye. Trimmed hard from Trace's renderer.ts, all flagged in gl/renderer.ts's own header comment: no GPU texture residency budget/eviction (a real concern for 'hundreds of photos' per RUMBO.md, deliberately deferred until the capture UI, task 2.3, produces real frame counts to profile against instead of guessing), no mesh skinning/rig, no adjustment layers, no selection, no pigment-mix wet blending (one ported brush.ts preset sets pigmentMix, but live stroke merging is the future drawing UI's job), no thumbnail downscaling (task 2.3 is the first actual caller). tasks.description: Save/resume a project (frames + layers + metadata) on local disk, no network. A stop-motion project is hundreds of photos — specifically test that closing and reopening the app loses nothing.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the app is closed mid capture session and reopened THE SYSTEM SHALL restore the project exactly as it was, frame by frame.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-08. Built ahead of 2.3 (capture UI) on explicit owner instruction, same kind of exception as 2.1/2.2: persistence logic doesn't touch the camera plugin or need a real shutter button to exercise it, only a document with cels in it (synthetic ones here, same reasoning as the 2.2 harness). 2.4 (export) was intentionally NOT started alongside this — it needs native AVFoundation/Swift work that shares phase 1's device-verification limitation (can write the code, can't build or run it from this environment), whereas 2.5 is fully browser/IndexedDB-based and testable here. IndexedDB chosen over Capacitor's Filesystem plugin (the owner's call) to avoid a new native dependency for v1; flagged as a real device-reliability question worth another look once actual on-device behavior can be observed. PNG encode/decode uses upng-js (already the library RUMBO.md's known-debts note pointed at) instead of Trace's canvas.toBlob() specifically so core/io.ts runs under npm test (no DOM/canvas in Node) — found and worked around a real decode bug in upng-js@2.1.0 along the way (auto-selected palette mode crashes toRGBA8; forced off via encode's undocumented 6th argument, forbidPlte). Split three ways per CLAUDE.md's gl/-is-the-only-WebGL-contact rule: core/io.ts (pure metadata + PNG, unit tested, 9 new tests in io.test.ts), gl/projectIO.ts (Surface <-> pixels glue), state/projectStore.ts (IndexedDB, degrades to a no-op under Node same as palettes.ts does for localStorage). Verified in a real browser via scripts/persistence-smoke.mjs (Playwright): save a synthetic two-cel-camera-layer + one-draw-layer project, reload the page (the closest proxy this environment has for force-quit + relaunch — no physical device), confirm every field and every composited pixel survives. Along the way this also caught and fixed a real aliasing bug in Renderer.renderDocumentFrame (task 2.2): its returned surface is a reused scratch buffer, so holding two frames' results at once silently corrupts the first — now documented on the method itself, not just fixed locally.

tasks.title: Drawing UI: canvas, pointer input, brush/color panels
tasks.description: Connect the already-ported brush.ts and the curated palettes to a real interactive canvas — pointer events (mouse/pen/touch) drive StrokeBuilder, stamps paint onto the active layer's cel via drawStamps, the result composites and presents live. Not originally itemized in this document (added retroactively on 2026-09-09): checkpoint.md's 2026-08-16 entry already flagged brush.ts as groundwork ported with no consumer yet, and this is that consumer. Single fixed draw layer, single frame — no timeline, no camera layer (that's 2.3, still blocked on device verification).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user drags a pointer across the canvas THE SYSTEM SHALL paint a visible stroke with the selected brush and color, and THE SYSTEM SHALL let the user switch brush or color between strokes without affecting ink already on the canvas.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-09. Owner asked what else could be added while phase 1 stays blocked; this was picked over two other camera-independent options (Firestore rules, the web half of export) as the highest-value one — the actual product differentiator, not backend plumbing. New gl/engine.ts is deliberately minimal, not a port of Trace's core/engine.ts: no revision/touch()/subscribe pub-sub (CLAUDE.md's documented pattern) yet, since the canvas is the only consumer so far and updates itself imperatively after every mutation — add the pub-sub once a second UI piece (layers panel, frame counter) actually needs to react to engine state, not before. No wet-stroke staging surface either (stamps go straight onto the permanent cel); no pigment-mix blending for the one brush.ts preset that wants it (Watercolor); no undo — all real, deliberate simplifications for this first slice, not oversights. Added erase-mode support to Renderer.drawStamps (blendFunc(ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) instead of the normal src-over) since brush.ts's two eraser presets need it and nothing had exercised that path yet. New state/tool.ts (active brush id + color, Zustand) split out the same way palettes.ts already is. Verified with real pointer events (not synthetic Stamp arrays) via scripts/drawing-smoke.mjs (Playwright): draws an actual stroke, confirms it's dark ink not blank paper; switches color and draws again, confirms the new stroke is the new color AND the earlier stroke is byte-for-byte unaffected; switches to the eraser brush and confirms it removes ink; confirms Clear resets the layer. All three Playwright smoke tests (renderer/persistence/drawing) still pass together — no regressions.

tasks.title: Bucket fill tool: tolerance, edge expansion, gap closure, reference-layer fill
tasks.description: Flood fill on the active draw layer, seeded at a tapped point: tolerance decides how different a color can still count as 'inside'; the fill bleeds a few pixels past the line to cover antialiasing (edge expansion/bleed); a real small break in the line doesn't leak the fill out (gap closure); the boundary is read from the whole composited document (any visible layer's ink), so one layer's lineart can bound a fill painted onto a different, active layer (reference-layer fill). Not originally itemized in this document (added 2026-09-10, owner request based on a reference video) — ported and extended from Trace's core/flood.ts + workers/floodFill.worker.ts.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user taps inside a closed ink outline with the bucket tool THE SYSTEM SHALL fill the enclosed area with the selected color, respecting the outline's edge; WHEN the outline has a small real gap THE SYSTEM SHALL still contain the fill instead of leaking past it; WHEN the active layer differs from the layer holding the outline THE SYSTEM SHALL still bound the fill by that outline while writing only to the active layer.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-10. Ported core/flood.ts near-verbatim from Trace (floodMatch, growFilled/edge-expansion, applyFillColor, extractRect) — but Trace's own shipped bucket tool turns out to only have tolerance + edge expansion, no actual gap closure: growFilled only grows the FILLED region after the fact, it never stops a flood from leaking through a real break in the line in the first place. Since gap closure was one of the two features explicitly asked for, built it for real rather than silently shipping half of what was asked: buildWallMask (inverse of floodMatch's tolerance test) + closeGaps (a genuine morphological close — iterated 3x3 dilate then erode, same iterative-radius style growFilled already uses) + floodOpenMask (scanline fill over the closed wall) — a real pipeline addition beyond what Trace has, not a redesign of what was ported. Renderer gained writeRect (sub-rectangle GPU write-back, sibling to the existing readRect). Engine.floodFill reads the reference from the whole composited frame (not just the active layer), so ink on any visible layer bounds the fill — the reference-layer-fill behavior — while writing only to the active layer's cel; Engine.activeLayerId, previously readonly, gained a setActiveLayer() method purely so this could be exercised at all (DrawingCanvas still only ever has one layer — no layers panel yet to pick an active one, a named UI gap, not a hidden one). No undo, consistent with the rest of the engine (see 2.6). Verified: 11 new core/flood.ts unit tests (including a synthetic case proving a real 1px gap leaks without closure and is contained with it) plus a new scripts/bucket-smoke.mjs driving real pointer-drawn outlines through the actual UI — basic containment, a real ~3px gap contained by default gapClose and proven to leak with gapClose=0, and a two-layer reference-fill scenario reading pixels off each layer's own cel directly. Building this smoke test surfaced and fixed two real bugs, neither a flood-fill defect: the UI's fill is fire-and-forget (async Worker round trip) so checks must poll the filled cel's surface.version instead of checking immediately or sleeping a guess; and brush.ts's ported One Euro smoothing filter has genuine steady-state lag behind constant-velocity motion, so a scripted drag that stops moving right at its target undershoots by several pixels — fixed by having the test dwell at each stroke's endpoint (a real hand naturally slows down there), not by changing the brush engine. All three prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, build, and lint all clean.

tasks.title: Undo/redo for strokes, bucket fills, and Clear
tasks.description: Wire the already-ported core/history.ts (task 2.1, unused until now) into gl/engine.ts so every mutating action on the active layer's cel — a drawn stroke, a bucket fill, Clear — is undoable and redoable, with UI buttons showing the pending action's label and standard keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl+Y). Not originally itemized in this document (added 2026-09-11, owner picked it over a layers panel or device verification as the next task).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user draws a stroke, fills an area, or clears the layer THE SYSTEM SHALL let them undo that action via button or keyboard shortcut and redo it afterward, restoring the exact prior pixels; WHEN a new action happens after an undo THE SYSTEM SHALL discard the redo stack.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Engine.beginStroke snapshots the whole active cel once (readRect over the full document) before any stamp is painted, then tracks only the dirty rect actually touched (expandRect per stamp, same padding Trace uses) so the Command stores just that sub-rectangle's before/after via extractRect — not the full cel — keeping undo memory proportional to what actually changed. This is coarser than Trace's own undo, which snapshots only the stroke's dirty rect from the start because it draws to a wet staging surface until pointer-up; this engine (task 2.6) stamps straight onto the permanent cel with no wet layer, so there's no untouched 'before' surface to read a precise rect from mid-stroke — a real, documented consequence of that earlier simplification, not an oversight here. Bucket fill uses history.run() (the action hasn't executed yet, unlike a stroke which already has by endStroke) with before/after computed from the flood worker's own returned sub-rect. Clear does a simple full-cel snapshot. A layer's cel is only created lazily (ensureCel, mirroring Trace's {cel, created} pattern) so undoing an action that created the first cel on an empty layer removes it entirely, not just paints it blank. UI: Undo/Redo buttons show the pending command's label (history.undoLabel/redoLabel) and disable correctly; DrawingCanvas subscribes to history.subscribe() inside the same effect that creates the Engine (a plain useState counter, not useSyncExternalStore — avoids a real ordering hazard where useSyncExternalStore's internal subscribe effect can fire before a separate effect that creates the subscribable object, missing the subscription on first mount). Bugs caught while building this: a self-caught no-op ternary in endStroke's label logic (read this.strokeBrush AFTER already nulling it a few lines above); a proactively-avoided ArrayBuffer detachment bug (postMessage's zero-copy transfer of target.buffer would have destroyed floodFill's own pre-fill snapshot had target.slice() not been taken before the transfer, not after). Verified via a new scripts/undo-smoke.mjs (Playwright): real pointer-drawn strokes, a real bucket fill, and Clear, each undone and redone through the actual UI (buttons and keyboard alike) — two independent strokes undo/redo in the correct order, a new stroke after an undo discards the redo stack, and a bucket fill's undo/redo round-trips correctly. Building it surfaced a test-methodology issue, not a product bug: the 'marker' brush preset is a chisel tip (aspect: 0.35), so its actual cross-stroke width is size(28) * aspect ≈ 9.8px, not the full 28px diameter assumed at first — a wide averaging box around the sample point was washing the thin line's darkness out into false negatives on presence checks; fixed by shrinking the sampling window to fit inside the known stroke width for presence checks specifically (same reasoning bucket-smoke.mjs already uses a small half for thin ink, e.g. checking the fineliner outline itself), while leaving the wider window on blank-paper checks since a wide box over empty paper is still reliably blank. All four prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Layers panel: add, delete, reorder, rename, visibility, lock, active-layer selection
tasks.description: UI to actually use the multi-layer document model that's existed since task 2.1 but had no way to exercise beyond a single fixed layer and a test harness calling setActiveLayer() by hand. Add/delete layers, reorder the stack, rename, toggle visibility and lock, and pick which layer strokes/fills write into. Not originally itemized in this document (owner picked it 2026-09-11, alongside starting Firebase and addressing engine drawing debts, all requested together — this is the first of the three).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user adds a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL make it the active one; WHEN the user deletes a layer (with more than one remaining) THE SYSTEM SHALL remove it and fall back to another active layer; WHEN the user hides a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it from the composite while leaving its pixels intact; WHEN the user locks a layer THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse both strokes and fills on it; WHEN the user reorders layers THE SYSTEM SHALL update the composite stacking order; WHEN only one layer remains THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to delete it.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Engine gained addLayer/removeLayer/moveLayer/setLayerVisible/setLayerLocked/renameLayer, all 'draw'-only (a camera layer's cels only ever come from the still device-blocked capture UI, task 2.3, so there's nothing meaningful for a panel button to add). removeLayer calls renderer.release() on each of the removed layer's cel surfaces immediately, since — unlike stroke/fill undo — layer removal isn't undoable, so nothing can still need that GPU texture afterward; this sidesteps a real gap that already exists elsewhere in the engine (a stroke/fill's created-cel undo keeps its Surface reachable for redo but never explicitly frees the GPU texture once the History entry itself gets trimmed by MAX_STEPS/MAX_BYTES — a pre-existing leak from tasks 2.6-2.8, not introduced here, and still open). Structural layer operations (add/remove/reorder/rename/visibility/lock) deliberately have no undo, unlike strokes/fills/Clear (task 2.8): a bare layer has no pixels for undo to meaningfully restore, and adding Command-based undo for array-splice operations on top of GPU-resource-holding Layer objects would reopen the same disposal-timing problem removeLayer's immediate release() was specifically added to avoid. This is also the point where CLAUDE.md's documented touch()/revision/subscribe() pattern (deferred at every engine.ts revision since task 2.6, each time noting there was no second consumer yet to justify it) finally gets built: the layers panel is that second consumer, and touch() lives inside renderAndPresent() itself (called at the end of every mutation already) rather than being sprinkled through every mutator by hand. Building this surfaced a real, separate bug worth its own line: Engine.beginStroke never checked layer.locked or layer.visible at all — only floodFill did (task 2.7) — so locking a layer through the new panel would have silently done nothing for strokes; fixed by adding the same guard beginStroke already needed on principle, not just to make the new UI feature work. Verified via a new scripts/layers-smoke.mjs (Playwright) covering: starting state (one active layer); add-layer making the new layer active; clicking a layer row to switch active layer; a stroke landing on whichever layer is active; rename via double-click-to-edit; hide/show actually removing/restoring a layer from the composite; lock genuinely blocking a stroke (not just a fill); reorder changing composite order; delete removing a layer and being refused (both via the disabled button and by calling removeLayer() directly) once only one layer remains. All five prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified alongside this one with no regressions; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Wet-stroke staging surface for non-erase strokes
tasks.description: Closes the drawing-engine debt flagged since task 2.6: stamps for a non-erase stroke now land on a scratch 'wet' surface for the whole stroke (composited live on top of the active layer's cel for the canvas preview) and only merge onto the permanent cel at endStroke, matching Trace's own approach, instead of painting straight onto the permanent cel as they arrive. Not originally itemized in this document (owner asked for this alongside the layers panel and starting Firebase, 2026-09-11; this is the second of the three, picked over also building pigment-mix blending itself in the same pass — see verify_note).
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user drags a non-erase stroke THE SYSTEM SHALL show it live on the canvas before the pointer lifts, without creating a cel on a previously-empty layer until the stroke actually ends; WHEN the pointer lifts THE SYSTEM SHALL merge the stroke onto the permanent cel with the same final pixels as before this change; WHEN the user erases THE SYSTEM SHALL continue to affect the permanent cel directly, unaffected by the wet surface.
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Renderer.renderDocumentFrame gained an optional wetOverlay param ({layerId, surface}), threaded into rasterizeLayer: when given and it names the layer being rasterized, that layer's cel (or a clear scratch surface, if the layer has no cel yet — the brand-new-layer case) gets `drawOver`'d with the wet surface into a scratch before taking part in the rest of the composite, using the renderer's existing copy/drawOver primitives — no new shader needed. Engine.beginStroke/paintStamps/endStroke branch on `!brush.erase`: non-erase stamps go to `renderer.scratch('wetStroke')` and only `drawOver` onto the real cel (lazily created via ensureCel, only if the stroke actually painted something) at endStroke; erase stamps still go straight onto the permanent cel throughout, unchanged from before this task, because erase's `blendFunc(ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA)` punches a hole in whatever is already there — routing it through an initially-transparent wet surface would erase nothing, then a normal drawOver merge would silently undo the whole gesture. This is exactly why Trace itself, and now this engine, don't put erase through wet staging either. A real, welcome side effect: undo's dirty-rect 'before' snapshot for a non-erase stroke can now be read right at endStroke, immediately before the merge, instead of reading the whole cel at beginStroke the way task 2.8 had to (the erase path still needs the old whole-cel read, since it never had an untouched pre-stroke surface to read from later). Standard alpha-blend compositing is associative for premultiplied 'over', so merging N stamps' accumulated wet-surface result onto the cel in one drawOver produces bit-identical pixels to painting the same N stamps directly onto the cel in sequence — confirmed by the unchanged pixel values across every pre-existing Playwright smoke test after this change, not just their pass/fail status. Pigment-mix blending (BrushPreset.pigmentMix, the MIX_FS shader gl/shaders.ts's own header comment already flagged as intentionally unbuilt) is still NOT implemented — this task only builds the wet-staging plumbing a future MIX_FS pass needs to hook into at the merge step; today's merge is plain drawOver regardless of pigmentMix, so Watercolor's pigmentMix: 0.15 still has no visible effect, exactly as before. Verified via a new scripts/wet-stroke-smoke.mjs (Playwright): a brand-new layer with no cel previews a stroke live before pointer-up and still has no cel mid-stroke; the stroke is visible both mid-drag and after merge; the permanent cel is created only by the merge; the eraser is confirmed to still act on the permanent cel mid-stroke (unaffected by wet staging). All six prior Playwright smoke tests re-verified with pixel values essentially unchanged (not just passing) — direct evidence the associativity argument holds in practice, not just in theory; 131 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-11. Pure CSS/JSX restyle, zero engine changes: new src/ui/drawing.css (plain CSS, not Tailwind — no such dependency exists yet and one screen doesn't justify adding one; dark palette keyed off #17171a/#121214 to match gl/renderer.ts's own WebGL clear color so the page doesn't clash with the canvas) and src/ui/icons.tsx (hand-authored inline SVG icons — no icon-library dependency, no emoji per the project's own UI-copy conventions; every icon is aria-hidden so it never contributes to a button's accessible name). Verified with a real screenshot (Playwright, both Draw and Bucket modes) before shipping, not just by reading the CSS — confirmed card sections, the segmented control's active state, circular swatches with a selection ring, and the brush chip rows' horizontal scroll with a fade-out mask hinting more content, all render as intended. tasks.title: Responsive layout: canvas stays fixed and visible across phone/iPad/desktop

New core/selection.ts (`polygonBounds`/`rasterizePolygon`/`maskContains`) rasterizes a closed path into a 0/1 mask via a pure-JS even-odd scanline fill — deliberately NOT the Canvas2D-based rasterizer Trace's own core/selection.ts uses (`ctx.fill()`, free antialiasing): that would break CLAUDE.md's 'core/ pure, no DOM' rule (Trace's own version of that rule already carries this one exception; Clumsyloop's doesn't), and this project's core/*.test.ts files run under plain Node with no DOM at all, so a canvas-based rasterizer couldn't be unit tested the way core/flood.ts already is — 7 new unit tests in selection.test.ts cover bounds-clamping, a filled square, a triangle covering roughly half its bounding box, a self-intersecting path not crashing, and point-containment. The trade-off is a hard (non-antialiased) selection edge, same reasoning core/flood.ts's own tolerance test already accepts for a fill boundary. gl/engine.ts gained `setLassoSelection`/`clearSelection`/`selectionContains` and the `beginMoveSelection`/`moveSelectionTo`/`endMoveSelection` trio: the move lifts the masked pixels into a floating buffer (cutting them from the permanent cel in place), previews the drag live via a scratch surface composited as an overlay — the SAME mechanism a wet stroke's live preview already uses, generalized by renaming `activeStrokeOverlay` to `activeOverlay` (a stroke and a selection move can never be in progress at once, being different tool modes, so there's no real conflict sharing that one overlay slot) — and pastes the result down via `drawOver` (proper alpha compositing) rather than `writeRect` (a raw overwrite), specifically so whatever was already at the destination outside the mask's shape survives instead of being clobbered by the floating buffer's transparent background. The whole cut+paste gesture becomes one undo step via a full-cel before/after snapshot, same cost tradeoff the erase stroke path already accepts, and a click with no actual drag is detected and skipped rather than recorded (reconstructs the identical cel exactly, proven by the cut-then-paste-at-the-same-spot math, so there's nothing meaningful to undo). New src/ui/DrawingCanvas.tsx wiring: a `'lasso'` tool mode (added to `state/tool.ts`'s `ToolMode` union) whose pointer handlers hit-test `engine.selectionContains` at pointerdown to decide 'start a new lasso' (outside) from 'grab the existing selection to move it' (inside) — the same convention any drawing app's lasso tool uses. The outline (both the in-progress path and the committed selection, dashed and animated as marching ants) renders in a new `<svg>` overlay sharing the canvas's own object-fit:contain-equivalent scaling via `preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"` matched to a `viewBox` of the document's own pixel size — deliberately NOT the manual scale/offset math `toSample`'s pointer-coordinate conversion needs (that direction, client-to-document, has no equivalent native browser primitive; this direction, document-to-screen for rendering, does). Two bugs caught and fixed while building this, both real: (1) a pure click-without-drag on the lasso tool would cut the selection's pixels away and never restore them, since the floating scratch surface was only populated by `moveSelectionTo`, which a plain click never calls — fixed by having `beginMoveSelection` place the floating buffer at its origin position immediately, not deferred until the first drag sample. (2) calling `setLassoSelection` (a real engine mutation that notifies other subscribed components, namely `Timeline`) from inside a `setLassoPath` functional state updater produced a genuine React warning ('Cannot update a component while rendering a different component') — updater functions must stay pure per React's own contract, since React may invoke them outside a plain event-handler context; fixed by reading the `lassoPath` state value directly instead. A third, purely cosmetic bug also caught by actually looking at a screenshot rather than trusting the code: the selection outline's white stroke was invisible against white paper (the default document background) — changed to the app's own accent blue, which reads against both a light canvas and the dark UI chrome. Deliberately out of scope for this v1, real follow-ups not oversights: a selection does NOT constrain painting when the user switches to Draw/Bucket (it only affects the lasso tool's own move gesture), no copy/duplicate (only move), no resize/rotate of the floating piece, and a moved selection can't be dragged partially off-canvas (clamped fully on-screen rather than clipping a partially-offscreen floating rect). tasks.description: Task 2.16's own verify_note named this as a real gap, not an oversight: every keyframe created so far uses `setKeyframe`'s default `easeInOut`, with no UI to change it. Picked up while continuing down the animation-engine backlog after keyframes and lasso.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the current frame has a keyframe for a transform property THE SYSTEM SHALL show an easing selector for it; WHEN the user changes that selector THE SYSTEM SHALL change only that keyframe's easing, leaving its value and every other keyframe untouched; WHEN this change happens THE SYSTEM SHALL make it undoable and redoable.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:keyframe-smoke && npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke && npm run test:renderer-smoke && npm run test:persistence-smoke && npm run test:timeline-smoke && npm run test:new-project-smoke && npm run test:lasso-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-12. New `Engine.getKeyframeEasing`/`setKeyframeEasing`, and a `<select>` in `TransformPanel.tsx`'s `TransformSlider` shown only when `hasKeyframeAtCurrentFrame` is true (nothing to attach an easing choice to otherwise). Building this surfaced a real bug, not in the new code but in how it interacted with an existing, deliberate one: `core/document.ts`'s `setKeyframe` intentionally ignores whatever easing is passed when UPDATING an existing keyframe, keeping its old one — a documented invariant (core/document.test.ts's own 'updating an existing keyframe keeps its previous easing' test), added so a plain value drag on an already-keyframed property (task 2.16's `previewLayerTransformValue`) can't accidentally reset a carefully-chosen easing back to the default. `setKeyframeEasing`'s first implementation went through `setKeyframe` anyway and silently did nothing, caught by a Playwright check that reads the actual keyframe's easing back from the engine (not just the DOM select's own value, which would have shown the same false-positive nothing-changed vs. actually-changed ambiguity) rather than trusting the dropdown alone. Fixed by mutating the found keyframe's `.easing` field directly instead of going through `setKeyframe` — a different operation from 'set/move a keyframe's value', so it's correct for this method specifically to bypass that invariant rather than change or route around it elsewhere. Verified by extending the existing scripts/keyframe-smoke.mjs (not a new script — this is a direct extension of the same Transform panel, not a separate feature): confirms a fresh keyframe defaults to easeInOut, changing the select updates only that keyframe's easing (not its value, not the keyframe count), and undo/redo both work as a single step. Re-verified the full pre-existing 11-script Playwright suite with zero changes needed beyond that one script's own extension. 138 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Selection-constrained painting
tasks.description: Named as an explicit scope cut in task 2.17's own verify_note: a selection only affected the lasso tool's own move gesture — switching to Draw/Bucket with a selection active didn't constrain painting to it at all. Picked up next in the animation-engine backlog, easiest to hardest, per the owner's own ordering.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a selection is active and the user draws, erases, bucket-fills, or clears THE SYSTEM SHALL only affect pixels inside the selection, leaving everything outside it untouched; WHEN a bucket fill is attempted starting from a point outside the selection THE SYSTEM SHALL do nothing at all, not partially fill the selection's interior through connectivity.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:lasso-smoke && npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke && npm run test:renderer-smoke && npm run test:persistence-smoke && npm run test:timeline-smoke && npm run test:new-project-smoke && npm run test:keyframe-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-12. New private `Engine.clipToSelection(rect, before, after)`: given a dirty rect's pixels before and after some paint operation, reverts anything outside the current selection back to `before`, returning `after` completely unchanged when there's no selection at all — the single mechanism behind all of this, applied after the fact to whatever `beginStroke`'s wet/erase merges, `floodFill`, and `clearActiveLayer` already computed, rather than trying to constrain the paint operations themselves (stamping, flood-filling) to the mask's shape directly. Simpler, and correct regardless of how complex the operation's own math is, since it works entirely on the same dirty-rect buffers this engine's undo system was already reading and writing. `clearActiveLayer` gained a whole second branch for the selection case (clearing only the masked pixels within the selection's own rect, not the full cel) instead of just running the existing full-cel clear through the clip function, since a full clear() call has no 'after' buffer of its own to clip — its 'after' is synthesized as an all-transparent buffer the same size as the rect, then clipped exactly like everything else. Building this surfaced a real, more interesting bug than a typo: a bucket fill's own flood algorithm is connectivity-based, not spatially local like a stroke — clicking OUTSIDE an active selection on a large connected blank-paper region could still flood color INTO the selection's own interior (since nothing walls off the mask boundary from the flood traversal itself), even though clipping correctly stopped the color from surviving outside the mask. `clipToSelection` alone only controls WHICH PIXELS may end up modified, not whether the fill should even run when its origin point isn't inside an active selection — fixed by rejecting the whole fill attempt up front (`if (this.selection && !this.selectionContains(x, y)) return;`) when the click itself falls outside the current selection, matching how a selection scopes everything else: a disallowed click does nothing at all, not 'only the allowed part happens'. Strokes don't need the equivalent guard — a stroke is spatially local (each stamp only paints within brush radius of the pointer path), so a stroke that starts outside the selection and drags into it already produces the right result purely from per-pixel clipping, with nothing to bleed through connectivity. Caught this exact bug via a Playwright check reading actual pixel values at a point deliberately placed away from any existing ink but still inside the selection, after a separate fill attempt from outside had already run — not by trusting that clipping alone would be sufficient. Verified by extending scripts/lasso-smoke.mjs (not a new script, since this is a direct extension of the same lasso/selection feature): a stroke and a bucket fill both respect the selection boundary in both directions (blocked outside, still working inside), and Clear only affects the masked area while a separate reference dot elsewhere on the layer survives untouched. Re-verified the full pre-existing 11-script Playwright suite with zero changes needed beyond that one script's own extension. 138 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.

tasks.title: Copy/duplicate a selection
tasks.description: The other explicit scope cut named in task 2.17's own verify_note: only a move existed, no way to duplicate a selection's pixels. Picked up right after selection-constrained painting, continuing the same easiest-to-hardest pass through the animation-engine backlog.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN the user duplicates an active selection THE SYSTEM SHALL create a copy of its pixels at a nearby offset location, leaving the original completely untouched; WHEN this happens THE SYSTEM SHALL make it undoable and redoable in one step, and the selection SHALL move to wrap the new copy.
tasks.verify_command: npm run test:lasso-smoke && npm run test:drawing-smoke && npm run test:undo-smoke && npm run test:bucket-smoke && npm run test:layers-smoke && npm run test:wet-stroke-smoke && npm run test:renderer-smoke && npm run test:persistence-smoke && npm run test:timeline-smoke && npm run test:new-project-smoke && npm run test:keyframe-smoke
tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-12. New `Engine.duplicateSelection(offset = 24)`: reads the selection's masked pixels (a plain copy, not a cut — the original cel is never written to at its own location, unlike `beginMoveSelection`), pastes them at a small fixed offset (clamped fully on-canvas, same clamping `moveSelectionTo` already uses) via `drawOver` so whatever's already at the destination outside the mask's shape survives, and moves the selection itself to wrap the new copy — so the very next drag (the existing move gesture, unchanged) can carry it further. A fixed, visible offset rather than pasting directly on top of the original: an exact overlap would be indistinguishable from a no-op both to the user and to any pixel-reading test, whereas an offset makes the duplication immediately observable. No-op if nothing inside the mask has any ink to begin with, avoiding a phantom undo step for duplicating an effectively-blank selection. New rail button (reusing `DuplicateFrameIcon`, the same two-overlapping-rectangles glyph the timeline's own duplicate-frame button already uses) next to Deselect, shown only when a selection exists, plus a Ctrl/Cmd+D keyboard shortcut. Verified by extending scripts/lasso-smoke.mjs: duplicating leaves the original ink in place, creates a copy at the exact expected offset, and undo/redo both work as one step. Re-verified the full pre-existing 11-script Playwright suite with zero changes needed beyond that one script's own extension (already updated together with 2.19 in the same pass, since both touch the same lasso feature and script). 138 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean. Still open, real follow-ups per task 2.17's own original list: no resize/rotate of a selection or its duplicate, and a moved/duplicated selection still can't be dragged partially off-canvas.

Built ahead of 3.1 on the same kind of exception already used repeatedly in phase 2 (2.5/2.6/2.7 built ahead of 2.3): 3.1 needs a real Firebase Console project and a physical device for Sign in with Apple, neither available in this environment, but the rules themselves are fully testable against the LOCAL Firestore emulator with no live project at all — `.firebaserc`'s 'demo-clumsyloop' project ID is the documented way to run the emulator suite standalone (Firebase treats any 'demo-*' project ID as emulator-only, never touching real GCP). firestore.rules covers exactly the three collections this task's own title names, not more: users/{userId} (publicly readable — the future feed needs to show a clip's owner — writable only by that user, to their own doc only), projects/{projectId} (read/update/delete gated on the EXISTING document's ownerId via `resource.data`, create gated on the INCOMING one via `request.resource.data`, since `resource` doesn't exist yet on create — a common real mistake in Firestore rules if both checks aren't kept distinct), entitlements/{userId} (read your own, write NONE at all — CLAUDE.md is explicit that only a Cloud Function's Admin-SDK write, which bypasses these rules entirely, is trusted; task 3.4 is what will actually perform that write). Verified via a new scripts/firestore-rules-test.mjs (16 checks against the real emulator, not a rules simulator): public read of a user profile, self-write allowed, cross-user write denied, unauthenticated write denied; project create/read/update/delete allowed for the owner and denied for a different user, including the create-with-spoofed-ownerId case; entitlement read allowed for the owner, denied for a different user, and write denied even for the owner themselves. tasks.title: Cloud Function: receipt validation → entitlement in Firestore
tasks.description: The client transaction is never trusted alone — the Cloud Function validates against the App Store Server API and only then writes the entitlement. Built ahead of 3.3 (device/App-Store-Connect-account-gated) the same way 5.2 was built ahead of 5.1's own UI half: the decision logic and the HTTP/auth plumbing need no real StoreKit client to be written and unit tested, only a fake App Store Server API response.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: WHEN a valid sandbox transaction is sent to the Cloud Function THE SYSTEM SHALL write the entitlement to Firestore; WHEN a tampered or fake transaction is sent THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it without writing anything.
tasks.verify_note: in_progress, not done — deliberately: one real, disclosed security gap remains (see below), so this cannot honestly be marked complete even though every other piece is built and tested. New functions/src/appStoreAuth.ts signs the ES256 JWT Apple's App Store Server API requires as auth (iss/iat/exp/aud/bid claims, kid header) using Node's own `crypto` module (`dsaEncoding: 'ieee-p1363'` gives the raw r||s signature JWS needs directly, no DER-conversion step, no added JWT-library dependency) — tested against a throwaway ES256 keypair generated at test time, since this project has no real App Store Connect credentials. functions/src/appStoreClient.ts calls the real endpoint shape (`/inApps/v1/transactions/{id}`, sandbox/production base URLs) with an injectable `fetchImpl` specifically so it's unit-testable without a real network call to Apple. functions/src/transactionPayload.ts decodes the JWS `signedTransactionInfo` Apple returns and validates its shape — but does NOT verify the JWS signature against Apple's certificate chain, a deliberate, clearly-disclosed gap (see that file's own header comment): full X.509 chain validation up to Apple's actual root CA is a meaningful piece of security-critical crypto that can't be safely eyeballed into existence without a genuine Apple-signed payload to test against, which no credentials in this environment can produce. Until that's added, `validateReceiptCallable` trusts whatever payload is embedded in whatever JWS it's handed — fine for exercising the entitlement-decision logic end to end with a fake payload, NOT safe to accept real payments with. functions/src/entitlement.ts is the pure decision (`decideEntitlement`: active unless expired or revoked, still resolves rather than rejecting for an expired/revoked-but-genuinely-parsed transaction, since a lapsed subscriber should correctly flip back to not-entitled rather than freeze). functions/src/validateReceipt.ts is the orchestration (fetch → decode → parse → confirm bundle ID → decide), throwing a single `ReceiptRejected` type for every failure mode (Apple refusing the transaction ID, a malformed payload, a payload for a different app's bundle ID) so `index.ts`'s `validateReceiptCallable` (an `onCall` HTTPS function) has exactly one thing to catch and turn into an `HttpsError`, writing nothing to Firestore in any of those cases — mirrors task 5.2's own 'thin runtime wrapper around plain, testable logic' shape. 29 unit tests total across the new modules (up from 5.2's 3), including tests named directly after this task's own acceptance criteria wording ('a valid sandbox transaction produces an active entitlement to write', 'a fake transaction ID is rejected, producing nothing to write', 'a tampered payload is rejected, producing nothing to write'). Along the way, fixed a real gap in functions/'s own tooling: its tsconfig originally excluded `*.test.ts` from `tsc --noEmit` entirely, meaning the 'lint' step never actually typechecked any test file — split into tsconfig.json (everything, used for typecheck/lint) and tsconfig.build.json (excludes tests, used for the real `npm run build` deploy artifact), and fixed the test-only loader hook (functions/scripts/ts-extension-resolve.mjs) to redirect a `.js`-suffixed import to its sibling `.ts` file when running against source directly, matching functions/'s NodeNext convention (real Node ESM, `.js` extensions even in `.ts` source, unlike the root app's bundler-resolution/extensionless-import convention) — also fixed the root eslint.config.js, which was linting functions/ under browser-oriented rules never meant for it (a plain `any` usage failed there that tsc's own stricter check didn't flag), by adding functions/ to the root config's own ignore list alongside dist/ios, since it's a separate deployable package with its own lint step. tsc, lint, and all 138 web-app unit tests remain clean; this task didn't touch any web app code. Still fully open: real App Store Connect credentials (a task 3.1/device-account concern), the JWS signature/chain verification gap named above, and task 3.5 (gating features on the resulting entitlement) itself.

tasks.description: Once a report threshold is crossed (to be defined, start conservative — 1 report is enough to hide while under review, not to delete), the clip stops appearing in feed queries without being deleted yet. tasks.verify_note: Passes as of 2026-09-12. New functions/ package (its own package.json/tsconfig.json, firebase-admin + firebase-functions as real dependencies, Node 20 target to match the actual Cloud Functions runtime): functions/src/moderation.ts is the pure decision logic (`REPORT_THRESHOLD = 1`, `shouldHideClip(reportCount)`), deliberately separated from any Firebase runtime so it's testable with plain `node --test` the same way this whole project's own `core/` modules are — reuses the exact same TS-loader trick (`register-ts-loader.mjs`/`ts-extension-resolve.mjs`, copied in rather than imported across package boundaries, since `functions/` needs to stay self-contained and independently deployable via `firebase deploy --only functions`). functions/src/index.ts is a thin Firestore-trigger wrapper (`onDocumentCreated('reports/{reportId}')`): counts existing reports for the new report's `clipId` and, once `shouldHideClip` says so, writes `clips/{clipId}.hidden = true` with Admin SDK privileges — the same field firestore.rules refuses to every client, by design. A malformed report (missing/non-string `clipId`) is a silent no-op, not a thrown error, since firestore.rules' own create rule for `reports` only validates `reporterId`, not `clipId`'s shape. 3 unit tests cover `shouldHideClip` at, below, and well past the threshold; `tsc`/`npm run build` both compile clean. Genuinely attempted a full Firestore-trigger integration test too (creating a real report doc against the Functions+Firestore emulators together and checking the clip actually gets hidden), not just the pure-logic tests — `firebase emulators:start --only functions,firestore` loads the function definition successfully ('Loaded functions definitions from source: onReportCreated') but then fails registering the Firestore trigger with a malformed-JSON error from what's very likely an emulator-suite/environment quirk specific to this sandbox (confirmed the proxy's own `noProxy` list already exempts 127.0.0.1/localhost, so it isn't the usual proxy-blocks-egress explanation this project hits elsewhere) — not a bug in the function's own code, which is a small, directly-readable use of well-established Firebase Admin SDK/Cloud Functions v2 patterns. Documented rather than silently skipped, same honesty bar as the camera plugin's 'written but unverified on real hardware' notes elsewhere in this file. Root firebase.json gained a functions emulator config (port 5001) and codebase declaration either way, so a real environment with working local emulator networking can run that fuller integration test as-is.
